replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is a statistical technique used to reduce the dimensionality of a dataset while retaining as much variability as possible. The first step is to standardize the data. Then, you compute the covariance matrix. Next, you calculate the eigenvalues and eigenvectors of the covariance matrix. The eigenvectors are the principal components, and the eigenvalues represent the variance explained by each principal component. You can then sort the eigenvalues in descending order and select the top k eigenvectors to form a matrix. Finally, you transform the original data into the new subspace using this matrix.
